# Building NebulaStream {#sec-app-build .unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note title="Status: complete first draft"}
:::

This appendix walks through three supported ways to build
NebulaStream from source: the Nix flake, the Docker development
container, and a local build with vcpkg. The official source of
truth is the README; this appendix summarises the steps in book
form for the reader who wants to build the engine while reading.

The toolchain requirements are stringent: **Clang 19** is the only
supported compiler. This is documented in CLAUDE.md; the Nix and
Docker paths take care of installing the right toolchain
automatically.

---

## A.1 The Nix flake {#sec-app-nix}

If you have Nix installed with flakes enabled, this is the path
of least friction:

```shell
# One-time IDE setup (also creates the cmake-build-debug directory)
nix run .#clion-setup

# Configure the build
./.nix/nix-cmake.sh \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug \
    -G Ninja \
    -S . -B cmake-build-debug

# Build everything
./.nix/nix-cmake.sh --build cmake-build-debug

# Run tests
./.nix/ctest --test-dir cmake-build-debug -j
```

The Nix flake (`flake.nix` at the repo root) pins every
dependency: LLVM 19, Folly, ANTLR4, simdjson, fmt, spdlog, and so
on. Builds are reproducible across machines.

For formatting and clang-tidy fixes:

```shell
nix run .#format
nix run .#clang-tidy
```

---

## A.2 The Docker dev image {#sec-app-docker}

If Nix is not available, the Docker development image is the next
best option. It uses the same toolchain pinned the same way:

```shell
# Build (or pull) the local development image
./scripts/install-local-docker-environment.sh

# Configure
docker run \
    --workdir $(pwd) \
    -v $(pwd):$(pwd) \
    nebulastream/nes-development:local \
    cmake -B cmake-build-debug

# Build
docker run \
    --workdir $(pwd) \
    -v $(pwd):$(pwd) \
    nebulastream/nes-development:local \
    cmake --build cmake-build-debug -j

# Test
docker run \
    --workdir $(pwd) \
    -v $(pwd):$(pwd) \
    nebulastream/nes-development:local \
    ctest --test-dir cmake-build-debug -j
```

The verbose `docker run` invocation can be aliased to a single
command in your shell config; the README has notes on doing so.

---

## A.3 Local build with vcpkg {#sec-app-vcpkg}

For a local build with neither Nix nor Docker, vcpkg manages
dependencies. The manifest is at `vcpkg/vcpkg.json`. You will
need:

- Clang 19.
- Ninja or another CMake generator.
- vcpkg installed and bootstrapped.

```shell
# Configure
cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug -G Ninja -S . -B cmake-build-debug

# Build
cmake --build cmake-build-debug -j
```

vcpkg will populate dependencies on first configure; subsequent
configures are fast.

---

## A.4 Build types and what they enable {#sec-app-build-types}

NebulaStream supports four build types, distinguished primarily
by logging and assertion behaviour:

| Build type | Logging | Asserts | Optimisation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Debug` | TRACE | enabled | none (`-O0`) |
| `RelWithDebInfo` | WARN | enabled | with debug info (`-O2 -g`) |
| `Release` | ERROR | enabled | full (`-O3`) |
| `Benchmark` | none | disabled | full + native (`-O3 -march=native`) |

Pick `Debug` when you are actively developing — TRACE-level
logging is usually what you want when something is wrong.
Pick `RelWithDebInfo` for performance work that still needs
asserts. Pick `Release` for production. Pick `Benchmark` only
for performance experiments where you understand exactly what
you are measuring.

The `cmake-build-instrumentation` directory referenced in
Chapter 21 is a separate build type for performance instrumentation
work; the team's CMake helpers handle it through the build type
mechanism.

---

## A.5 Common targets {#sec-app-targets}

A few build targets you will use repeatedly:

```shell
# Build everything
cmake --build cmake-build-debug -j

# Build a single module
cmake --build cmake-build-debug -j --target nes-query-optimizer

# Build the systest binary
cmake --build cmake-build-debug --target systest

# Build the worker process
cmake --build cmake-build-debug -j --target nes-single-node-worker

# Build the REPL and CLI
cmake --build cmake-build-debug -j --target nes-repl nebuli

# Format the entire codebase
cmake --build cmake-build-debug --target format

# Check format without modifying
cmake --build cmake-build-debug --target check-format
```

The `format` and `check-format` targets are required to pass
before any PR can merge.

---

## A.6 Running tests after building {#sec-app-tests}

Cross-reference Chapter 20.

```shell
# All tests
ctest --test-dir cmake-build-debug -j --output-on-failure

# Tests matching a regex
ctest --test-dir cmake-build-debug -R "DecideJoinTypesTest" --output-on-failure

# Single systest
cmake-build-debug/systest/systest -t nes-systests/operator/join/JoinMultipleStreams.test

# Single systest in interpreter mode
cmake-build-debug/systest/systest \
    -t nes-systests/operator/join/JoinMultipleStreams.test:1 \
    -- --worker.default_query_execution.execution_mode=INTERPRETER
```
